rubric.why: Identifies hypertext as text that contains links.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning links within or attached to text.

rubric.why: Explains what the links connect to or allow the user to do.
rubric.description: Explains that the links lead to other documents or pages.
rubric.how: Award for identifying linked pages/documents or navigation between them.

modelAnswer: Hypertext is text that contains links to other documents or web pages.
These links allow users to move from one page or document to another.

items.followUp: What information is placed inside the body section of an HTML page?

rubric.why: Identifies the body section as the part containing the page's content.
rubric.description: States that the body section contains the web page's content.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the body as the content section.

rubric.why: Explains that the body content is displayed to the user in the browser.
rubric.description: States that the content is displayed in the browser.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning that the page content is shown or visible in the browser.

modelAnswer: The body section contains the main content of an HTML web page.
This content is displayed in the browser and is written between the <body> and </body> tags.

items.followUp: Define a logical proposition and give one example.

rubric.why: Identifies a Boolean proposition as a statement.
rubric.description: States that a Boolean proposition is a statement.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as a statement or declarative sentence.

rubric.why: Gives the defining property of a Boolean proposition.
rubric.description: States that it has a truth value of true or false.
rubric.how: Award for specifying that it is either true or false.

modelAnswer: A Boolean proposition is a declarative statement that has a truth value.
It is either true or false, but not both.

items.followUp: What are the two possible truth values of a proposition?

rubric.description: Names true as a truth value.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a proposition may be true.

rubric.why: Identifies the other possible truth value.
rubric.description: Names false as a truth value.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a proposition may be false.

modelAnswer: The truth value of a proposition is its logical status.
It is either true or false.

items.followUp: What does ASCII stand for, and what is it used for?

accept: american standard code for information interchange
rubric.why: Provides the correct expansion of ASCII.
rubric.how: Award for the complete correct name.

rubric.why: Explains that ASCII assigns codes to characters.
rubric.description: States that ASCII represents characters using numeric codes.
rubric.how: Award for explaining the character-to-code representation.

modelAnswer: ASCII stands for American Standard Code for Information Interchange.
It is a coding system that represents letters, digits, symbols and control characters using numbers.

items.followUp: What is the base of the binary number system, and which digits does it use?

rubric.why: Identifies the base of the decimal system.
rubric.description: States that the decimal number system has base 10.

rubric.why: Identifies the digits used in the system.
rubric.description: States that decimal uses the digits 0 through 9.
rubric.how: Award for listing or specifying the range of decimal digits.

modelAnswer: The decimal number system is a positional number system with base 10.

rubric.why: Identifies sabotage as an intentional act.
rubric.description: States that sabotage is deliberate or intentional.
rubric.how: Award for indicating that the act is done on purpose.

rubric.why: Identifies the computer-related target or effect of sabotage.
rubric.description: States that sabotage damages or disrupts a computer system, data, network or services.
rubric.how: Award for naming an appropriate computer-related target or disruption.

modelAnswer: Sabotage is the deliberate act of damaging or disrupting a computer system, network or its data.
It may prevent the system or its services from working properly.

rubric.why: Explains the legal protection or rights provided by copyright.
rubric.description: States that copyright gives legal protection or exclusive rights to the creator or owner.
rubric.how: Award for identifying copyright as legal protection or a set of exclusive rights.

rubric.why: Identifies the restriction copyright places on copying or using a work.
rubric.description: States that copying or using the work without permission is prohibited.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning unauthorized copying or use.

modelAnswer: Copyright is the legal protection given to the creator or owner of an original work.
It gives them rights over its copying, distribution and use, and prevents others from doing so without permission.
